title: Sweet Is the Time of Spring
description: Sweet Is the Time of Spring in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 745 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Youth and the Spring-time”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sweet is the time of spring, When na-ture's charms ap-pear; The birds with cease-less plea-sure_ sing, And hail th'o-pen-ing year: But sweet-er far the spring Of wis-dom and of grace, When child-ren bless and praise their King, Who loves the youth-ful race.

lines: Sweet is the time of spring,
The birds with ceaseless pleasure sing,
When children bless and praise their King,
Sweet is the dawn of day,
When light just streaks the sky;
When shades and darkness pass away,
When doubt and darkness are withdrawn,
And decks each plant and flower we view,
When there the dew of youth is seen
